message:
I am thinking...: Now I can see the structure. Let me focus on cases where printSrcIdx is called AFTER another operand has already been printed (so op_count > 0).

Looking at case 16 (CMPSB):
```
printSrcIdx8(MI, 1, O);   // Op=1
SStream_concat0(O, ", ");
printDstIdx8(MI, 0, O);   // Op=0
```

In CMPSB, `printSrcIdx8` is called first (with MCInst operand index 1). At that point, `op_count` is 0 (no operands have been added yet), so `access[0]` is read. Then `printDstIdx8` is called with op_count=1.

But wait, looking at cases 26-28 (LODSB, OUTSB, etc.):
```
printSrcIdx8(MI, 0, O);
return;
```

These just call printSrcIdx with op_count starting at 0. So access[0] is read, which is fine since get_op_access always initializes access[0].

Let me look at the MOVSB case. In case 23:
```
printDstIdx8(MI, 0, O);  // INSB, MOVSB, SCASB, STOSB
```
This just prints the destination. But MOVSB also has a source operand...

Wait, let me look more carefully at where printSrcIdx is called with operand index 1 (meaning MCInst operand 1, not op_count). Let me check line 33078:
```
33078:    printSrcIdx8(MI, 1, O);
33083:    printSrcIdx32(MI, 1, O);
33088:    printSrcIdx64(MI, 1, O);
33093:    printSrcIdx16(MI, 1, O);
```

Let me look at the context of these.
